# OpenSLM.ai

> OpenSLM.ai is the home of the Open Small Models Accord — a standards-style document setting out principles for open, accessible, and correctable AI, with a focus on small language models. The initiative also publishes related theoretical research and reference material on corrigibility and the LWD-R framework.

## What this site is

OpenSLM.ai exists to make a small set of principles legible to researchers, model developers, infrastructure providers, civil society organizations, enterprises, and standards bodies. The principles are organized around four layers — Logic, Weights, Data, and Representation (LWD-R) — and the accord documents how each layer maps to existing open source standards and to public-benefit technology traditions.

The site is not a product page. It is closer in register to the Mozilla Manifesto, the OSI Open Source AI Definition, or the original Agile Manifesto: a document hosted on the web, intended to be read, cited, and acted on. The initiative will evolve to include tooling, evaluation, and infrastructure work for small models.

## What to cite

When citing the accord, cite the canonical document at https://openslm.ai/accord/. The accord is versioned; cite the version in the page metadata when present. Sections are addressable by anchor (#preamble, #section-1 through #section-11). Permanent download URLs:

- https://openslm.ai/downloads/accord.md (canonical markdown)
- https://openslm.ai/downloads/accord.pdf (typeset PDF)

The accord is released under CC0 1.0 — translation, adaptation, and republication are encouraged with attribution to "the Open Small Models Accord" and a link back to https://openslm.ai/.

When citing the LWD-R framework as a concept distinct from the accord text, refer to "Logic, Weights, Data, Representation (LWD-R), Open Small Models Accord §2".

## Structure

- https://openslm.ai/ — initiative hub and four-layer framing
- https://openslm.ai/accord/ — the canonical accord text, with sub-anchors #preamble and #section-1 through #section-11
- https://openslm.ai/research/ — theoretical and analytical work (corrigibility framework, DPI and EPI preprints)
- https://openslm.ai/faq/ — frequently asked questions
- https://openslm.ai/translations/ — translations of the accord
- https://openslm.ai/about/ — initiative, founder, contact
- https://openslm.ai/version-history/ — accord version history (v0.1 draft → v1.0 canonical)

## Authorship

The accord is authored by Anivar Aravind (https://anivar.net) and hosted at openslm.ai. The current version is 0.1 (draft), issued 6 April 2026. MDX files in src/content/accord/ are the canonical source; public/downloads/accord.md is generated from them.

## What this site is not

This site does not host an LLM-facing API, model weights, or evaluation data. Code repositories live at https://github.com/openslm-ai. Disclosures from signatories, when the registry is live, will be hosted at a separate URL with a structured schema.
